findings.now: That happens once your heart rate climbs above its usual resting rate, or the time between its beats varies less (a smartwatch shows both), and it lasts until you calm down.
So if you try to process trauma while you're above this red line, you're adding to the armor instead of taking it off.

Above the line your functional IQ drops a lot, and stress chemicals called catecholamines flood the Nucleus Accumbens, a reward center deep in the brain, where they switch on DeltaFosB, the protein researchers suspect holds the armor in place.
